correctness.rationale: The zero-right-hand-side BDF2 formula gives Δ_n = R_n² Δ_(n−1)/(1+2R_n), so Z is a positive sum of products of the multipliers a,b. Their product is r/[(1+2r)(r+2)]<1. Equal limiting state frequencies (including deterministic alternation) give log-product rate log(ab)/2<0 and almost-sure absolute summability. Write A=a^s, B=b^s and M=diag(A,B)P for the two-state transition matrix P. Expected s-powers of products are components of iterates of M; exponential decay when ρ(M)<1 gives a finite moment by Minkowski for s≥1 and subadditivity for 0<s<1. Conversely finite conditional moments obey m>Mm from the strictly positive additive term 1, whence a positive left Perron vector gives ρ(M)<1 even for the irreducible two-cycle at p=0. The determinant at 1 is 1−AB−p(A+B−2AB). The other eigenvalue is <1: M is diagonally similar to a symmetric matrix whose smaller eigenvalue is at most pB<1. For a≤1, all row sums are ≤1, one strictly smaller; irreducibility gives ρ<1. For a>1, the determinant decreases from 1−AB>0 to (1−A)(1−B)<0 and hence gives precisely the displayed cutoff and divergence at equality. Substitution gives 24/31 and 171/283 at r=3, bracketing 7/10. At p=0 the two phase sums are (1+a)/(1−ab) and (1+b)/(1−ab). The degenerate r=1 uses two labels for the same physical ratio; the deterministic Z=3/2 is independent of p. This is an infinite-iteration startup-amplification statement, not a finite-horizon mesh-stability result. The frozen check script was inspected, not run; it samples the algebra and is not needed for the proof.

evidence: Theorem 1.4 gives E|Z|^s<∞ iff E|W|^s<1 and E|Q|^s<∞ for iid affine pairs (W,Q), assuming nonzero multiplier, nontrivial additive term, and no deterministic common fixed point.
Arbitrary-grid BDF2 stability theorems use finite intervals and startup derivatives; they do not establish the unscaled infinite-iteration moment statement.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The perpetuity theorem covers the target once grouped; for a>1 and 0<p<1 the cycle multiplier has both W>1 and W<1 with positive probability, and Q>0, so no common deterministic fixed point exists. The finite-horizon BDF2 results are not used for this implication.

evidence: High and low run lengths H,L are independent geometric variables with success probability 1−p. One cycle has W=a^H b^L and additive reward Q=1 plus its proper-prefix products, so Q≤sum_{k<H}a^k+a^H/(1−b). If a>1, E[Q^s]<∞ exactly when pA<1 (the prefix a^H is included). In that domain E[W^s]=(1−p)²AB/[(1−pA)(1−pB)]. Requiring this to be strictly below one is exactly 1−AB−p(A+B−2AB)>0; equality diverges, and outside the domain the moment cannot be finite.

For a≤1 the cycle has W<1, with Q bounded by a linear function of H and consequently all finite-order moments; p=0 is a deterministic geometric sum. Negative drift and finite logarithmic reward moments follow from the geometric runs. The r=3 witness evaluates the same criterion at s=1,2.

The frozen statement gives no distinct BDF2 mechanism or stability conclusion beyond that specialization.
